changes: HOTFIX — update wallvault is repaired: the vault archive is AES-256 encrypted (compression method 99), which Info-ZIP's unzip cannot verify or extract — every run died with 'The download is not a valid zip' even though the payload was intact. The deployment now uses the 7-Zip backend (7z): full integrity verification, decryption with the archive key, and extraction are handled natively

New: update wallvault pass <key> stores the archive decryption key in ~/.cache/fedora-mactahoe/wallvault.conf (chmod 600); without a stored key the tool prompts silently (no echo) at run time. update wallvault <link> [key] registers a custom endpoint and optionally the key in one call

Hardened transfer: HTTP errors now fail the download (curl -f), transient interruptions auto-retry (3 attempts) plus one full automatic retry of the entire transfer, and a truncated payload is caught by the 7z integrity test instead of producing misleading errors
Clear failure diagnostics: wrong decryption key vs corrupt payload vs missing 7zip backend are now reported as distinct errors with the exact remedy

Professional-grade output: all wallvault UI copy was rewritten in a corporate/data-center register — asset bundle, authorized transfer, integrity verification, staging, credentials persisted, operation aborted
7zip added to the RPM Packages step (step bumped so every machine installs it on the next update)

HOTFIX — the ( TAG ) now lands in the log filename on EVERY path. 3.5 stamped install.sh-created logs, but the bootstrap one-liner (curl|bash) creates the log itself and hands it to the installer — so those files came out untagged. Bootstrap now computes the same tag (BASH for the one-liner, UPDATE-FULL / UPDATE-QUICK when the updater drives it) and stamps it into its own log name, keeping filename and installer header consistent
update quick dropped its 8-second loading ritual — quick means quick. It now runs exactly like menu [1]: straight to the incremental update, no prompts, no spinner
Both fingerprints re-pinned (bootstrap.sh and update.fish changed)

Every install/update run now stamps WHO ran it into the log filename: FedoraTahoe_log.<date>.<time>.<ID> ( TAG ).txt — ( BASH ) for the curl|bash one-liner, ( MANUAL ) for running install.sh directly, ( UPDATE-QUICK ) / ( UPDATE-FULL ) / ( UPDATE-CONFIG ) and one tag per target (UPDATE-ICONS, UPDATE-THEME, UPDATE-FONTS, UPDATE-SOUNDS, UPDATE-EXTENSIONS, UPDATE-GDM, UPDATE-WALLPAPER, UPDATE-PFP, UPDATE-GTK, UPDATE-VIDEOS, UPDATE-SERVICES, UPDATE-DEFAULTS, UPDATE-DCONF, UPDATE-NOTIFIER, UPDATE-CLEAN, UPDATE-WALLVAULT) for the updater

The same tag appears in the log header box (new Method row), is saved into install-state.json (source field) and shows up in the update log history — one quick look tells you how every run was started
New command: update quick — the incremental update with your saved answers, no prompts, straight from the shell (identical to menu [1])

HOTFIX — installs no longer die at 'RPM Packages'. Two codec package names in the v3.2 driver batch did not exist on Fedora 44 (gstreamer1-plugins-good-extra and gstreamer1-plugins-bad): dnf rejected the whole 43-package transaction, so every fresh install and every update rerun of that step stopped with 'No match for argument'. They're replaced with the real packages — gstreamer1-plugins-good and gstreamer1-plugins-bad-free (with -freeworld and -free-extras already installed from the RPM Fusion step) — and the full transaction was dry-run verified to resolve: 43 names, all found, zero errors
Step version bumped so every machine re-runs the repaired RPM Packages step on the next update
New: update wallvault (aliases: update wall, update w) — the 500+ wallpaper vault, downloaded right from your terminal

Free and private: a one-time 6-digit code is shown in the terminal (no email, no account), you type it and the ~623 MB vault downloads behind a live braille spinner — then it's verified, unzipped and landed in ~/Downloads/Wallvault-Pack, temp files cleaned up
Safe by design: 3 code attempts with a 10-minute expiry, Ctrl+C aborts the download and leaves nothing behind
Custom link: update wallvault <google-drive-link> points the vault at any file you own — the link is saved in your private cache (chmod 600) and used for every future download
update wallvault help box added to per-target help, the usage box and the menu ([16] wallvault)

Your settings are safe forever — installs and updates no longer overwrite your personal config: PATH lines you added to fish (set -gx PATH, fish_add_path, fish_user_paths) are migrated once into conf.d/50-user-path.fish and never touched again. The opencode-style path wipe is gone
Kitty gained user.conf — a file of your own that installs and updates never touch; put anything you like there and it survives every refresh, always winning over the theme

Media & hardware drivers built in: Intel Media Driver + VA-API (hardware video on Intel/AMD), the full GStreamer codec suite (libav + good-extra + bad + ugly), Mozilla OpenH264, ALSA SOF firmware for modern laptops
Storage & sharing: NTFS-3G read/write for Windows drives, Samba client + CIFS utils so the smb function works out of the box
Printing: cups-filters + HPLIP driver stack
Emoji picker: Super+. opens GNOME Characters — pick emoji anywhere, no setup needed
update.fish re-pinned with a fresh fingerprint

Per-target help: update <target> help shows a dedicated box for every part of the update — what it does, what it asks, its flags and whether a fresh session is needed. update help <target> works too, and the main help lists both. 16 targets covered (icons, theme, fonts, sounds, extensions, gdm, wallpaper, pfp, gtk, videos, services, defaults, dconf, notifier, clean, menu). Read-only: never prompts, never downloads, never touches your setup

HEIC image support — now built in. Fedora MacTahoe 3.0 introduces native HEIC/HEIF decoding: open Apple's photo format directly in your GNOME Image Viewer, see thumbnails in Files, and convert anytime with heif-convert. No new apps, no viewer changes — your iPhone photos just work. Powered by libheif-freeworld (RPM Fusion free, already enabled by the installer) plus the heif-tools conversion suite. Fresh installs get it out of the box; existing setups can grab it with: sudo dnf install libheif-freeworld libheif-tools
update wallpaper and update pfp now offer a Both option: pick 3 in the pack picker to wipe BOTH packs (normal + +18 folders and XMLs) and re-download them fresh in one go
update wallpaper both also works as update wallpaper both — same for pfp
help box gained update wallpaper both / update pfp both rows
update services now ALWAYS asks about firewalld — it checks the live state first (FIREWALLD IS RUNNING / FIREWALLD IS OFF box) and asks every time instead of silently reusing the saved answer
turning firewalld OFF is now the default everywhere: pressing Enter in update services or the installer's firewalld question disables it (was No/keep before)
the installer's firewalld prompt now defaults to Yes — press Enter to disable and save ~30-50 MB

fix update wallpaper / update pfp ignoring your pick: the saved answer from the original install (+18) was overriding the choice you make in the picker, so picking Normal still downloaded the +18 pack. Env vars passed by update <target> now always win over saved answers (saved answers still apply on full installs and when the target passes nothing)
same fix protects update gdm, update videos and update services — their forced settings can no longer be overridden by an old saved answer

fix incremental updates getting stuck: a machine installed on an older version stored per-step versions as that overall version (e.g. 2.2), which is higher than today's per-step manifest values (1.x) — every step was skipped and the version never moved. Now an older overall version forces all steps to re-run, then normal per-step gating resumes
update help redesigned: gradient title, diamond section tags, aligned two-column command table (bold white names, bold gray descriptions), tag-cloud toolbox, divider footer
all help text is now bold so it stays readable on light auto-theme backgrounds
fixed command-row width so the box right edge is a straight line
the recovery warning is now BIG and bold: a red ERROR/RESCUE/WARNING banner replaces the fish welcome when the config is missing, and the instructions are bold
the guard message is refreshed on existing machines automatically via update configs (same marker-replace mechanism)

- A tiny system-wide rescue detector now guards 'update': if ~/.config/fish/functions/update.fish is ever deleted, the /etc copy detects it, explains the missing dependencies and offers to download the latest update function (yes is the default, 5 tries, fingerprint-verified) — the updater never runs until the user copy is restored
update configs replaces the old system-wide copy with the rescue detector — /etc/fish/functions/update.fish is now the tiny detector, the full updater lives only in ~/.config/fish/functions/
- update configs now refreshes the did-you-mean command handler in /etc too — a wiped fish config still suggests command fixes (it was the only nice thing missing after a reset)

- no more silent skips: when the sudo cache is cold, update configs pops the polkit password dialog (pkexec) once and copies the system-wide fish helpers (rescue detector + did-you-mean handler) anyway — cancel and it tells you it skipped

- the did-you-mean fallback loads from /etc/fish/config.fish whenever your own handler file is gone (fish won't autoload event handlers from /etc by itself) — wiped configs still suggest command fixes
- the recovery warning in every terminal is now plain language: 'type update, press Enter' — no more wall-of-text one-liner (update configs refreshes it on existing machines too)
Quick updates are now truly quiet — no more questions: your saved answers are reused (Discord, wallpapers, videos) once you've answered them once
- Picker validation messages (Invalid/Cancelled) now go to stderr, keeping command-substitution output pure
- update wallpaper add / update pfp add (also --add, -add) install the other pack alongside — without the flag the chosen pack replaces the other (folder + XML)
All setup prompts moved from bootstrap into the installer — bootstrap is just the start button now: splash, verify, download, hand off
Discord's answer is now saved too (it was the only prompt without persistence)
Bootstrap no longer prints its own system-info box — the dashboard shows once, from the installer
Bootstrap no longer prints its own SECURE TUNNEL box — the tunnel shows once, from the installer
Tunnel location is hidden — a generic 'Location: Secure' row instead of fake CDN node details
The installer download now shows a live progress bar — the clone runs quietly in the background, no more raw git text
The download progress bar now matches the updater's loader — braille spinner, rotating status, [███░░░] bar with real percent (re-pinned bootstrap fingerprint)
Fixed the download progress bar crashing on the first tick (grep no-match tripped the ERR trap under set -euo pipefail); percent now only moves forward
Fish config backups keep the same 5-snapshot limit as dconf (was 10) — 6th and older auto-deleted on every config apply
The start screen waits 60 seconds max — no key press and bootstrap closes itself (just run it again when you're ready)
Closing bootstrap early (Ctrl+C forced exit or the 60s auto-close) leaves no log behind — the temp log is deleted, since nothing ran
Running install.sh directly now behaves the same: every wait and yes/no question auto-closes after 60s of silence, and closing it early (Ctrl+C twice or the timeout) deletes the log too
A closed installer is no longer reported as a failure — the updater says 'closed before finishing' and you just run it again when ready
Fixed the crooked log-header box (blank rows and data rows now line up with the 62-wide border) and the 'More from Eprahemi' box (links no longer poke past the right edge)
The kitty one-liner no longer bursts out of its box — it's now shown as a clean code line under both warning boxes (bootstrap + installer)
Deep-scan cleanup: removed dead code (unused _save_prompt_answers_all, stray _rc captures, unused PINK color in bootstrap) and re-pinned the bootstrap fingerprint
Fixed kitty terminal boxes: ✦/⚠ title rows padded correctly for narrow glyphs; removed leftover over-padding on the "Press any key" rows
The update menu no longer lists every step that will re-run — just what's new, then the choice. Cleaner.
Fixed the progress bar showing '�' blocks — the bar builder used tr (byte-based, mangles multi-byte █); now built with string concat like install.sh's sed bars, byte-perfect in any locale

MacTahoe GTK source is now vendored in the repo (vendor/MacTahoe-gtk-theme) — if the upstream repo is ever deleted or unreachable, the theme still compiles fresh for your GNOME version, and GDM + Firefox theming still work via the vendored tweaks.sh

The firewalld question moved up front — it now appears with the Discord/wallpaper/video prompts before Phase 1, so the installation never pauses mid-flow; the actual disable (or keep/enable) still happens in the 'Disable RAM-wasting Services' step, and your answer is saved like the others

update menu — per-target toolbox: re-run a single part of the setup with update <target> (icons, gtk, extensions, wallpaper, pfp, theme, fonts, sounds, videos, services, gdm, defaults, dconf, notifier, clean) — no full reinstall needed

update <target> asks about logging out when the change needs a fresh session — per-target reason in the box (theme/gtk/extensions/gdm/wallpaper/icons/fonts), strict y/n with no default so Enter alone never logs you out
Every update fetch now shows a live braille spinner while cloning — same style as the installer's loader, no more static 'Fetching...' text
Ctrl+C is now safe everywhere: cancelling mid-install or mid-fetch prints '✘ Cancelled — nothing was changed.', never touches your setup, and cleans up the temp files
Fixed the download spinner never noticing a failed clone (fish's wait always reported success) — git's real exit code is read from the temp bundle now, so connection errors are reported honestly

Self-healing 'update' command — if update.fish is ever deleted (say, a wiped fish config), the boot + 2-hour updater timer restores it automatically, fingerprint-verified against the pinned sha256 so unverified code is never installed
System-wide rescue copy — the installer keeps a root-owned copy of update.fish outside your home folder: even with the entire fish config wiped, the 'update' command still answers

update configs now refreshes every config location — kitty, fish (config + all 40 functions), starship, GTK, fastfetch, systemd units AND the update notifier (script + timer): every folder is created if missing, every file overwrites if present, and your fish config is auto-backed up before any override
update configs also keeps the system-wide rescue copy current — done silently, without asking for a password or printing anything extra
update configs no longer leaks ktheme's raw error if the wallpaper file ever goes missing — the live re-theme is fully silent now
update configs confirms with '✓ Rescue copy (system-wide) updated.' only when the system-wide copy was actually refreshed (warm sudo window); with no cached credentials it stays silent and skips
Security hardening pass — the full audit is in:
Verified update chain — installs are fingerprint-checked, tamper-proof downloads, a trust prompt the first time, hard refusal on any mismatch
Your settings are safe — a full dconf snapshot is saved before anything touches your GNOME settings (restore with one command)
gdm wallpaper switching no longer uses shared /tmp — everything stays in your private cache
Kitty control sockets are private now — no other user can connect to your terminal
Automatic security downloads — patches download in the background nightly (never installed without your say-so)
Backup snapshots are private too — folder and files locked to you only
Fish config safety net — every config refresh auto-backups your live fish folder first (last 10 snapshots kept)
The can't-lose-it guard — a root-owned warning in the system fish config: if your fish config is ever deleted, every terminal shows the exact one-line recovery

Kitty follows your wallpaper — ktheme pulls the colors out of your desktop picture and re-themes every kitty window, live. A quiet background watcher does it automatically every time the wallpaper changes (ktheme on/off to control it)
Kitty Colorful Edition — a fresh full palette, interactive kittens (ctrl+shift+f4 themes, ctrl+shift+d diff) and remote control from any terminal
hint — a little teacher in your terminal: shortcuts, functions, the palette, and live demos, all in one menu
fastfetch shows your terminal; old kitty/fastfetch config backups cleaned up
New Fish function: smb — full Samba file sharing manager (setup, users, shares, passwords, data export, service control)
Updated 18+ wallpaper pack with new backgrounds
